metadata.note: The Pontiac, Oxford and Northern - the 'Polly Ann' - Pontiac - Caseville, Michigan (~100 mi through the Thumb), and the GTW's Cass City - Bad Axe branch (18.5 mi). Opened Oct 1883 by the Pontiac, Oxford and Port Austin; reorganised 1889 as the Pontiac, Oxford and Northern; operated by the Grand Trunk Western from 1909 (or 1910) as its Cass City Subdivision and merged into it 1928; passenger (by then mixed) service ended 31 Dec 1955. The Bad Axe branch carried mixed trains 1913-1951. Research report: research/branches/pontiac_oxford_and_northern_railroad.txt.

metadata.operator_split: Main line: Pontiac, Oxford and Port Austin 1883-1889 | Pontiac, Oxford and Northern 1889-1909 | Grand Trunk Western 1909-1955, three features sharing identical geometry (Rule 4). Not split: the 1888-89 mortgagee-in-possession period (same trains, same name), the 1928 PO&N-into-GTW merger and the 1923 CN takeover of the Grand Trunk (GTW ran the trains throughout). Bad Axe branch: GTW throughout (built by its Detroit and Huron subsidiary).
metadata.omitted: Report block [5], GTW Boblo excursion trains Caseville - Detroit in the 1960s: drawable NONE (no year sourced). Freight-only after 31 Dec 1955 (Rule 1), the GM Lake Orion plant spur, and the never-built Caseville - Port Austin and Pontiac - Detroit extensions.
metadata.existing_layer_note: No existing layer drew this corridor. Grand Trunk Western colour pulled programmatically from data/detroit_flint.geojson ('Grand Trunk Western Railroad', #264653). The report's side finding - data/grand_trunk_sarnia_detroit.geojson 'Grand Trunk: International Limited' in #0d7377 - is a separate Rule 4 issue not touched here.
not_yet_sourced: GTW takeover year CONFLICT: 1909 (abandonedrails 'came under GTW control'; en.wikipedia/Polly Ann Trail Management Council 'began operating the line in 1909'; Fowler 'Pontiac Yard 1909') vs 1910 (michiganrailroads.com 'control passed to the GTW in 1910'). Drawn 1909 by majority as the shared transition year of pon-pontiac-caseville and gtw-cass-city-subdivision; the court sale (adjourned to 19 Nov 1908) was not found. Passengers ran continuously either way - only the colour of 1909 is in doubt.

Frequencies on every segment are estimates: no PO&PA, PO&N or GTW public timetable times were read (the Feb 1952 Guide table is not legible in the OCR). Whether the GTW train was mixed throughout or only late is not established.

Bad Axe branch start: opened Sept 1913, depot 1914; passenger carriage in 1913 is inferred, so 1914 is drawn. The michiganrailroads.com story's 'short 48 year life' conflicts with 1913-1951 (38 years); the 1951 end is dated by the timeline entry.
The month of the 1889 PO&PA -> PO&N reorganisation is not established.
The PO&N's first ~2 mi out of downtown Pontiac (and its own Pontiac depot) are not mapped in OSM or OHM and are drawn as a straight leg.
1960s GTW Boblo excursions Caseville - Detroit: no year (GTWHS newsletter Spring 2002 is the lead); not drawn.

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap + OpenHistoricalMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror and overpass-api.openhistoricalmap.org, 2026-11-03), routed with opstrace.py. old_railway_operator probed over the corridor for GTW / Grand Trunk / PO&N / Pontiac, Oxford spellings: only 'GTW' (108 ways) and one 'Grand Trunk Western Railroad' way exist, nearly all of them on the Holly, Pontiac Belt and Mount Clemens subdivisions and other GTW trails (treated as foreign track here); the only GTW-tagged ways on this road are the 'Cass City Spur' (live/disused, north Pontiac - Lake Orion). No PO&N or Pontiac, Oxford spelling is tagged in OSM. Made of, south to north: straight chord downtown Pontiac - north Pontiac (see geometry_quality); OHM way -202182427 'Pontiac, Oxford and Northern Railroad' and the OSM GTW Cass City Spur to Lake Orion; the OSM Polly Ann Trail (abandoned railway) Lake Orion - Oxford - Leonard - Dryden - Imlay City - Lum, with short OHM PO&N stretches where the trail leaves the grade (Oxford village, ~2 mi in all); OHM 'Pontiac, Oxford and Northern Railroad' Lum - North Branch - Kingston - Wilmot; OHM 'Pontiac, Oxford and Port Austin Railroad' Wilmot - Deford - Cass City - Gagetown - Owendale - Pigeon - Caseville.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 99.5 mi Pontiac - Caseville against 100.59 mi documented main line (MCR-1903 via michiganrailroads.com), 99.4 mi (GTW Cass City Sub employee timetable), 99.7 mi (Fowler line 140) and 99.894 mi (ICC valuation via abandonedrails). Made of: 97.3 mi traced on the road's own grade (about 33.7 mi OSM Polly Ann Trail, 3.6 mi OSM GTW Cass City Spur, 60 mi OpenHistoricalMap PO&N/PO&PA ways, which are hand-drawn historical lines rather than surveyed track). ONE STRAIGHT-LINE LEG: downtown Pontiac (Holly Subdivision at OSM node 62219749, near the GTW station / 'PO&N Junction', Fowler MP 0.1) due north to the south end of OHM way -202182427, 2.2 mi - neither OSM nor OHM maps the PO&N's first ~2 mi out of Pontiac, so the exact street-grid alignment and the PO&N's own Pontiac depot (Fowler MP 0.3) are not drawn; the routers' alternative (west along the GTW Holly Subdivision and back east on the Pontiac Belt, 1909+) was rejected as another line. All 16 station waypoints lie within 0.9 km of the drawn line (Pontiac is the straight leg's downtown end). No relocation of the line is documented; the same alignment is drawn for 1883-1955. The Cass City Spur part reflects the modern GTW track, assumed to be on the original grade.

segments.note: Opened through Pontiac - Caseville in October 1883: track laid Pontiac - Imlay City in May 1883, a passenger train reached Caseville on 3 Oct and the line was completed / first through train on 8 Oct 1883 (michiganrailroads.com 1883 timeline, citing MHM and MRRC; en.wikipedia Polly Ann Trail). Listed in the 1884 Official Guide (Fowler 'q' tags at Watrous and Winsor, later Owendale and Linkville). Projected to Port Austin, hence the name, but never built beyond Caseville. From 15 Mar 1888 the mortgagee, Farmers' Loan and Trust Co., took possession and operated the road under the same name until the 1889 foreclosure (not split: no separate public identity). Ends 1889 as an era only - the reorganised Pontiac, Oxford and Northern continued the trains (feature pon-pontiac-caseville); the month of the 1889 change is not established. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (no PO&PA timetable was read).
sources: Segment-level: research report research/branches/pontiac_oxford_and_northern_railroad.txt block [1] - start from the michiganrailroads.com 1883 timeline (3 and 8 Oct 1883) and en.wikipedia Polly Ann Trail; end is the 1889 foreclosure/reorganisation (michiganrailroads.com PO&PA and PO&N pages, abandonedrails). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: The 'Polly Ann' (also 'Poor Old and Neglected', Flint Journal 21 Nov 1908 via en.wikipedia), successor by the 1889 reorganisation of the Pontiac, Oxford and Port Austin. In 1903: 100.59 mi main line, 22 stations, 7 locomotives; new Cass City depot and Caseville turntable 1902 (Michigan Commissioner of Railroads 1903 via michiganrailroads.com). In receivership from March 1905. Ends 1909 when the Grand Trunk Western took control and began operating the line (abandonedrails; en.wikipedia via the Polly Ann Trail Management Council) - michiganrailroads.com says 1910; see not_yet_sourced. 1909 is drawn as the shared transition year with feature gtw-cass-city-subdivision. Passenger trains are implied by the 1903 station and depot figures and the road's reputation for poor passenger service, but no PO&N public timetable was read: dates are the corporate dates. headway_min is an ESTIMATE.

segments.note: Grand Trunk Western operation of the former PO&N, its Cass City Subdivision (99.4 mi in the GTW employee timetable). GTW control from 1909 (abandonedrails; en.wikipedia) or 1910 (michiganrailroads.com) - see not_yet_sourced; the PO&N company was merged into the GTW in 1928, which did not change who ran the trains. GTW agents at Oxford, Cass City and Caseville in 1917. The Feb 1952 Official Guide (schedules of 25 Nov 1951) prints a GTW 'PONTIAC-CASEVILLE' table and indexes every station on the line without the freight-only mark. Passenger service - by then one of Michigan's last mixed trains - was withdrawn on 31 Dec 1955 (michiganrailroads.com 1955 timeline, citing MDOT and the Michigan Railroads Club newsletter of July 1975; en.wikipedia 'Passenger service ended in 1955'). Freight continued: Kings Mill - Caseville closed 1984, most of the rest in the 1990s, not drawn (Rule 1). Annual GTW Boblo excursions from Caseville in the 1960s are not drawn: no year is sourced. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (roughly one train each way daily; the 1952 Guide's times are not legible in the OCR).

properties.line: Grand Trunk Western: Bad Axe Branch
properties.speed_source: estimated: single-track Thumb branch line with many stops, mixed train in its later years; no running times were read. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap way -198826563 'Detroit and Huron Railroad' via overpass-api.openhistoricalmap.org (2026-11-03), routed with opstrace.py from the junction vertex on the main line.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 18.5 mi Cass City (junction on the main line south of the Cass City depot) - Bad Axe against 18.5 mi documented (Fowler line 141, MP 74.4 - 92.9). Entirely on OpenHistoricalMap way -198826563 'Detroit and Huron Railroad' (a hand-drawn historical line; the branch was lifted after 1951 and nothing of it is mapped in OSM). No straight-line legs. The branch ends where the OHM way ends, on the south-east side of Bad Axe (~0.45 km from the town-centre geocode); the GTW depot site was not located separately.

segments.note: Cass City - Bad Axe, built 1913 by the GTW's Detroit and Huron Railroad (the 'D&H branch') and opened in September 1913; Bad Axe GTW depot built 1914, GTW agent there in 1917 (michiganrailroads.com Bad Axe station page). Drawn from 1914, the first year with a passenger depot at Bad Axe: carriage of passengers in 1913 itself is inferred, not stated. 'Mixed train service through much of its short ... life'; GTW abandoned the branch on 30 Apr 1951 (michiganrailroads.com 1951 timeline, citing MRC 3/1987 and 8/1988), and the last train that day carried 'a combine car on the rear for passengers' (michiganrailroads.com story 'The Last GTW Train To Bad Axe - 1951') - so here the closure date is the passenger end. headway_min is an ESTIMATE.
